This timeless romance begins, as the best do, in a windswept castle at the foot of a mighty mountain. As soon as you catch a glimpse of Inverlochy Castle, it’s love at first sight.
Our beautiful 19th century castle near Fort William is a place that speaks to those who know, with its tasteful rituals, storied antiques and deeply sophisticated atmosphere. Step over our threshold and be smitten by the quiet splendour.
Book A Table
DINING
From the exquisite ritual of afternoon tea to the seasonal sensations of Seasgair and the togetherness of our Mary Shaw table, at Inverlochy, dining is always sublime.
Find US
Our iconic Highland setting between mountain and loch feels exclusive and remote, yet at just three miles from Fort William, it’s refreshingly easy to get here.
Book A Room
STAY
Richly decorated, tasteful spaces with just a touch of drama. Set your stay in the peaceful walled garden room or in the castle. A Highland haven awaits.
EXPERIENCES
Get out into the fresh Highland air, connect with nature or try something entirely new with an activity in or around the hotel. Adventure awaits.

Indulge in the ultimate foodie experience: a demonstration or dinner hosted by the Michelin-starred master of classical French cooking, Michel Roux Jr.

Home Stay
Stay
Our luxurious rooms and suites are scattered around the main castle building and gardens. Each timeless space has been thoughtfully curated to honour the romance and sophistication of this traditional 19th century castle. Step over the threshold, close the door behind you and feel part of something truly special.
CASTLE ROOMS & SUITES
Revel in the antique pieces and timeless textures of these individually designed spaces. Offering uninterrupted views of the grounds and loch, each room is a luxurious, authentic delight.
WALLED GARDEN ROOMS
Overlooking our peaceful walled gardens, these eight rooms in the converted stable block offer all the character and charm of our castle rooms, plus a balcony or terrace.
GATE LODGE
Nestled in the castle grounds, this intimate lodge house offers a secluded space a short walk from the castle at the front entrance, with one double and one single bedroom.
Go beyond your room
Our rooms and suites are wonderful places to spend time, but there’s plenty to experience if you do venture out and explore. Nestled in the foothills of Ben Nevis, the area surrounding Inverlochy Castle is rich in landscape and history, from the falls at Glen Nevis to the Glenfinnan monument and the dramatic scenery of Glencoe.
Stop and smell the flowers in our magnificent walled garden or explore the many secret paths that wind their ways through the trees. Or, if you prefer the great indoors , why not try our fabulous cuisine with our ‘Seasgair’ experience by the world-renowned Michel Roux ?

Home About
About
Welcome to Inverlochy Castle Hotel, a beautiful 19th-century Scottish castle, near Fort William in the Highlands of Scotland.
Being in Scotland's finest Country Hotel, you will enjoy the holiday of a lifetime, where every detail for your comfort and enjoyment has been carefully considered and one which you are sure never to forget.
The area surrounding Inverlochy Castle is rich in landscape and history, to name but a few of these breath-taking places - the falls at Glen Nevis, the monument at Glenfinnan and the mountains of Glencoe. During a trip to Balmoral in 1873, Queen Victoria spent a week at Inverlochy sketching and painting where she wrote in her diaries 'I never saw a lovelier or more romantic spot'. Nestling in the foothills of the mighty Ben Nevis, Inverlochy Castle sits amidst some of Scotland's finest scenery.

Home Hotel Sustainability Policy
Hotel Sustainability Policy
At Inverlochy Castle, we are committed to promoting environmental, social, and economic sustainability in all aspects of our operations. Our goal is to minimize our environmental footprint, enhance community engagement, and provide responsible hospitality for our guests.
Environmental Commitment
Energy Efficiency : We strive to reduce energy consumption by ensuring regular maintenance of energy appliances, and smart systems where available for heating, cooling, and lighting control.
Waste Management : We aim to reduce, reuse, and recycle waste materials. We actively promote responsible waste disposal practices.
Sustainable Procurement : We prioritise purchasing, locally sourced food, and biodegradable materials where possible to reduce our carbon footprint.
Community Engagement & Social Responsibility
Local Partnerships : We collaborate with local businesses, farmers, and artisans to support the local economy and provide guests with authentic experiences.
Employment Practices : We uphold fair labor practices, provide training opportunities, and ensure a safe and inclusive work environment for all employees.
Guest Awareness & Participation
We encourage guests to participate in our sustainability initiatives, such as reusing towels and linens.
Compliance & Continuous Improvement
We comply with all relevant environmental laws and regulations.
Staff are trained on best practices in sustainability, and we continuously seek innovative solutions to enhance our environmental and social impact.
At Inverlochy Castle, we recognise our responsibility to protect the planet and contribute positively to society. Through ongoing commitment and collaboration, we strive to create a sustainable and enjoyable experience for our guests, employees, and the community.
This policy serves as a framework for our sustainability initiatives. We welcome feedback and ideas from our stakeholders to further enhance our commitment to a greener future.

wikipedia.title: Inverlochy Castle Hotel
wikipedia.extract: Inverlochy Castle Hotel, formerly known as Inverlochy Castle, is a 19th-century baronial mansion near Fort William, Scotland. It is located about two miles away from the 13th century Inverlochy Castle, after which it was named. This is a baronial mansion was built in 1863 by William Scarlett, 3rd Baron Abinger, soon after succeeding his father as Baron Abinger in 1861. Queen Victoria spent a week at Inverlochy during an 1873 visit to Balmoral, remarking "I never saw a lovelier or more romantic spot". The house and estate were sold in 1944 to a Canadian entrepreneur, Joseph Hobbs, the owner of the nearby Ben Nevis distillery. Upon inheriting the estate, Hobbs' son converted the house into a hotel, which opened for the first guests in 1969.
